# Example Co

> A one-line description of what this company does

Two or three sentences an answer engine can quote verbatim: what the company does, for whom, and the one thing that makes it different.

## The numbers on this site

Every figure published on example.com is sourced in
`src/data/facts.json` in the site repository, and this file is generated from
that same source at build time. Nothing is estimated: a figure that cannot be
sourced is not published.

## Blog

- [How this template's SEO machinery works](https://example.com/blog/how-the-seo-machinery-works): A tour of the SEO plumbing this template ships with — canonical URLs, JSON-LD, sitemap, RSS and OG cards — and which file each piece lives in.
- [Writing content that answer engines actually cite](https://example.com/blog/writing-content-answer-engines-cite): The three evidence-backed GEO levers — citations, quotable definitions and front-loaded answers — and how this template's schemas force you to use them.

Index: <https://example.com/blog> · Feed: <https://example.com/rss.xml>

## Glossary

Reference definitions. Each entry carries a short definition written to be
quoted, its authorities by name, and a `retrieved` date where a URL was
checked. Where a figure is jurisdiction-specific or unverified, the entry says
so rather than publishing a number.

Core Web Vitals · llms.txt
